about: “Meum ac vestrum” modifies the singular “sacrifícium”: “my sacrifice and yours”. The response asks the Lord to receive it “de mánibus tuis” — from the priest's hands — for the glory of His name and the good of those present and of the whole Church. The rubric directs the priest to say the invitation with his voice raised a little and the closing “Amen” in a low voice.

seg.nr: The priest kisses the altar, turns to the people, spreads and joins his hands. The priest raises his voice only for the words “Oráte, fratres” and says the rest silently.

seg.tr: Pray, brethren, that my sacrifice and yours may be acceptable to God, the almighty Father.

fn.w001: A plural imperative addressed to those present.
fn.w002: Vocative plural, identical in form to the nominative and accusative plural.
fn.w007: A singular noun modified by “meum” (w004) and “vestrum” (w006).

seg.nr: The server answers, or those present. If there is no one to answer, the priest says the response himself, saying meis — my — for tuis.

seg.tr: May the Lord accept the sacrifice at your hands for the praise and glory of His name, for our good also and the good of all His holy Church.

fn.w014: A third-person subjunctive expressing a prayer.
fn.w019: Agrees with “mánibus” (w018) and refers to the priest's hands.
fn.w025: A reflexive possessive referring to “Dóminus” (w015) and agreeing with “nóminis” (w024).
fn.w030: Totíusque combines totíus with the enclitic -que (“and”), which places the stress on the preceding syllable.

seg.nr: The priest says Amen in a low voice.
